The style guide's quick check (Laura's four rules), for the new ground and cracks
  • Soft outlines? Yes: every new shape's rim is its own colour a shade darker, thin and see-through. The pillows are the game's own.
  • A light top and a deeper foot? Yes: the ground, the snow drifts, the doormat, the pebbles.
  • Drawn lines still crisp? Yes: the sign, the portrait's cord and the door are untouched.
  • Rich colour? The ground and cracks yes (warm earth; blue shade on snow). The pillows keep the fort's pale cream and lilac (a richer pillow would be Laura's pass).
  • Does it look like it lives next to the trike? It is the game's own pillow, more of it, on ground drawn by those rules.

FPW-Q1 · What shows through the cracks?

Pick: Dirt. Or Snow, or nothing (the deep shadow). Dirt keeps the pillows standing out, keeps the colour rich, and matches Camp Snugg.

FPW-Q2 · Where does the wall stand?

Pick: its foot near the bottom (a thin strip of ground). Or where it stands today (a taller strip; a quarter of an iPad).

FPW-Q3 · What do you see as the wall parts?

Pick: Camp Snugg's warm light, then the park, on today's timing. Or Camp Snugg itself behind the halves: a bigger change, its own follow-up card.

FPW-Q4 · The cushion doormat before the door?

Pick: keep it.
